attributes.nuance_translation: A casual way of expressing but, with the focus on giving reasons, elongating a pause, or leaving something unsaid due to awkwardness.

attributes.body:
んだけど is an expression that combines んだ (explaining/giving cause), with けど (but). Together they translate simply as 'but...', although the nuance is actually closer to 'but with (A) as the reason… (B)', while (B) is sometimes left unsaid. This implies that the speaker is looking for a reply, or does not want to say the (B) part of the sentence out of politeness/awkwardness.

There are several different forms of this construction that are mostly interchangeable with each other. From most casual, to most formal, they are as follows:

んだけど、んだけれど、んだけれども、んだが、んですが

ん may be replaced with の in any of the above expressions. However, it will again make it slightly more formal.

Caution

んだが, or simply だが is probably the 'strongest' out of these possibilities, and is considered quite masculine. If you are going to use this form, we recommend making sure that your tone is a bit softer, so that it does not sound too authoritative.

Fun Fact

ん (or の) may sometimes be omitted completely, but this is not so common in modern Japanese.

attributes.description: Explanatory の / んだ / んだけど / んですが

attributes.body: Both express contrast, but が is more formal and used in writing, like 面白いが難しい ('It's interesting, but difficult'). When combined with ～んだ・～んです, as in 行きたいんですが, it softens the sentence and invites a response or action from the listener.

Both introduce contrast, like the English 'but'. けど・だけど are common in speech, as in 難しいけど面白い ('It's difficult, but interesting.'). Adding ～ん to this pattern adds an explanatory nuance, often used to imply a request or hesitation, e.g. 難しいんですけど 'It's difficult, but...(do you want me to do it anyway?, etc.)'.

～んです・のです adds an explanatory tone to a statement, like 難しいんです ('It's difficult, I'm telling you.'). When paired with contrastive particles like けど or が, the speaker often implies something left unsaid, as in 難しいんですけど ('It's hard, but...', implying 'and that's why I can't do it', etc.).
